explain.say: Open a fridge and you'll see shelves, but does it matter what goes where? Yes! Look at the fridge on the board, starting with the top shelf. That's for food that's ready to eat, like leftovers and cooked dishes, so nothing raw can drip onto it.

explain.say: Look at the bottom shelf. This is where raw meat and fish go, covered in a box. Why? Raw meat can carry germs, and its juices can drip. Down here, drips can't land on food you'll eat without cooking. And cold air sinks, so it's often the coldest shelf.

faq.q: What goes on the top shelf of the fridge?
faq.a: Ready-to-eat foods, like leftovers, cooked meals and snacks. They're kept high up so nothing raw can drip onto them.
asks: Where do leftovers go in the fridge?

faq.q: Why does raw meat go on the bottom shelf?
faq.a: Raw meat and fish can carry germs, and their juices can drip. Covered on the bottom shelf, they can't drip onto food that won't be cooked.
asks: Where should I put raw chicken in the fridge?

faq.q: What is the salad drawer for?
faq.a: It holds fruit and vegetables and keeps the air around them a bit more humid, so they stay crisp for longer.

faq.q: Which part of the fridge is warmest?
faq.a: The door, because it swings out into warm air every time it opens. It suits drinks, jams and sauces better than milk.
asks: Should milk go in the fridge door?

faq.q: Why is the bottom of the fridge often coldest?
faq.a: Cold air is heavier than warm air, so it sinks to the bottom of the fridge.

facts: Food safety agencies advise storing raw meat and fish covered on the bottom shelf of the fridge.
Cold air sinks, so the lower shelves of a fridge are often the coldest.
